doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Working with Benny Goodman and what Goodman was like
summary: He played tenor with Goodman, who wanted him recorded, and describes a lonely, music-obsessed man.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I played tenor with him. But I’d given him some tapes of me playing clarinet and he never said a word about these. However I found out after he died from the president of the record company that he was with at the end, Music Masters, that he wanted them to sign me up and he would produce a record for me. But they didn’t — well we never heard of this guy you know — and then I went with Concord and I’m playing a job and the president of the record company shows up and he says, “I just wanted to tell you we could kick ourselves because Benny really wanted us to record you.” And I knew nothing about this until after he died.

He was a tight-lipped guy. He’s not the evil person that you’ve heard in a lot of books or interviews. He was a complex guy. I think he really didn’t know how to deal with his fame. He was uncomfortable about it and I think almost his whole life revolved around music, to the exclusion, unfortunately, of thinking about people’s feelings and things like that. But he just was obsessed with music. He practiced all the time. He was always thinking about those old Fletcher Henderson charts, how can I play them and make them sound fresh. And he did too. At the end we had a great band. But I think he was a very lonely guy. And I got pretty close to him at the end. We would go out to lunch all the time and I still have some phone messages from him and letters and things like that. I miss him, I do. The last band that was with him I think he had genuine affection for and we had affection for him. We respected him and we were there trying to play his music
